correctness.rationale: Hering--Maclagan Proposition 2.5 guarantees a positive grading for any actual edge; matching maximal weighted standard-monomial degrees gives (d-2)(u-v)=0 and hence standard grading. Opposite lex initial generators force nonzero pure quadratic coefficients and both x^d,y^d in the ideal. A length-2d homogeneous regular sequence gives I=(f,x^d), and dehomogenizing only the degree-d vector space proves that t^d is scalar modulo g. Characteristic zero excludes repeated nonzero roots, so their ratio is a nontrivial d-th root of unity whose trace lies in K. The explicit quadratic converse, rational trace classification, and Euler-totient lower bound yield the exact field criteria and sharp degree. The actual bundled checker and independent symbolic Gröbner sample evaluations verify examples but are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Field-dependence of Hilbert-scheme torus edges is a motivating obstruction in Hering--Maclagan, not an arbitrary numeric feature. Replacing a single d=5 example with an exact characteristic-zero field criterion yields infinitely many Q/R discrepancies and a sharp arithmetic invariant: the least number-field degree needed for the edge. For odd d this depends only on the smallest prime factor, a structural cyclotomic obstruction with explicit attaining fields. It addresses rational realizability for a natural uniform family that the complex geometric classification does not resolve arithmetically; it does not claim a new complex edge or an arbitrary extension beyond the motivated family.
